A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PredFormer and its nine transformer configurations. All 15 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison of text, equations, tables and figures despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original PredFormer experiments on Moving MNIST, TaxiBJ and WeatherBench, including architecture comparisons, component ablations and prediction visualizations.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds Human3.6m evaluation, additional baseline comparisons and a model-depth study.

M1.justification: The nine architectures, SwiGLU blocks, sinusoidal position encoding and L2 objective remain. However, v3 Table 3 explicitly adds a skip connection around each PredFormer layer for the Human3.6m Triplet-TST and Triplet-STS variants to stabilize training.

E1.justification: v3 adds Human3.6m human-motion video prediction using 256×256 RGB frames and four-frame input/output sequences. This substantially extends coverage beyond v1's synthetic digits, traffic heatmaps and temperature fields. The original three datasets remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated OpenSTL-ViT and OpenSTL-Swin comparators on all three retained benchmarks, providing direct comparisons with transformer-based temporal translators. SwinLSTM also enters the Moving MNIST and TaxiBJ tables. PredNet additionally participates in the new Human3.6m comparison; these are evaluated comparators, not merely citations.

E3.justification: Moving MNIST reporting changes from patch sizes 4/8 and 200/2000 epochs to patch size 8 and 2000 epochs, with all nine variants and an added depth sweep. Human3.6m introduces its own protocol, including PSNR and LPIPS evaluation. The stated inference-timing GPU changes from A5000 to A6000, preventing direct interpretation of cross-version FPS differences as methodological gains.

E4.justification: v3 Table 6 adds a two-to-eight-layer TSST scaling study. Conversely, v1's Moving MNIST patch-size/convergence analyses and its Moving MNIST SwiGLU/position-encoding ablations disappear. WeatherBench and TaxiBJ component and regularization ablations remain. The abrupt-traffic-change case remains in the supplement rather than being newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Results remain point estimates; uses of 'significant' do not introduce statistical testing.

E6.justification: v3 adds Human3.6m results, additional 2000-epoch architecture results and depth-scaling scores. Human3.6m TSST obtains MSE 110.9 versus SimVP's 115.8 and PredRNN++'s 110.0, showing mixed metric rankings. The retained 24-block, patch-8 TSST Moving MNIST MSE changes from 12.5 to 12.4. The 200-epoch and patch-4 results disappear. TaxiBJ and WeatherBench prediction errors remain unchanged for retained models, while FPS values change under revised timing hardware.

T1.justification: The attention, SwiGLU, residual-block and prediction-objective equations retain their mathematical substance. Supplementary Eq. 5 supplies reshaping pseudocode for an existing binary variant, following transformation illustrations in v1 Figure 4; it introduces no new theoretical assumption, derivation or result.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a convolution-free, recurrent-free gated-transformer framework with nine configurations. v3 removes the explicit 'first pure transformer' priority claim, extends the performance claim to four benchmarks, and replaces v1's 51.3% Moving MNIST headline with 48% plus faster-inference claims under its revised experimental presentation.

C2.justification: v1's detailed interpretations linking patch size and prediction horizon to spatial-versus-temporal variant rankings are largely removed. v3 develops depth-scaling interpretations, applies its CNN performance-ceiling argument to newly evaluated hybrid comparators, and adds human-motion interpretations. The qualifications about small-data overfitting and dataset-dependent variant choice remain.

D1.justification: v3 supplies Human3.6m preprocessing and hyperparameters, including batch size 8, 50 epochs and 12 GTB blocks, and revises the hardware description. It replaces v1's memory-related patch-4 exceptions with the narrower Moving MNIST configuration and re-documents reshaping for Binary-ST. Both versions still promise release of code and trained models.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Human3.6m and Latte references, discusses Latte's attention factorization, and expands positioning against the already-cited Earthformer. It also withdraws the explicit first-pure-transformer claim. The main related-work categories and most cited works remain.

P1.justification: v3 retitles and consistently reframes the paper around video prediction, rewrites the abstract and substantial experimental discussion, reorganizes the benchmark sections, and restructures the appendix into supplementary Sections 6–9. This constitutes substantial narrative revision beyond terminology replacement.

P2.justification: v3 adopts two columns, removes the opening performance chart, rearranges architecture panels, replaces the two Moving MNIST tables with one, and adds Human3.6m and depth tables. It splits the existing prediction figures and moves WeatherBench visualization into the main text. Table 5 incorrectly labels retained WeatherBench RMSE values as SSIM with an upward arrow.

improvement.justification: Human3.6m evaluation, direct hybrid-transformer comparisons and the depth sweep strengthen evidence for applicability and scalability that v1 supported less directly. This is a limited net improvement: v3 removes useful Moving MNIST analyses and introduces a WeatherBench metric-label error. Moreover, timing hardware changes while baseline FPS values remain unchanged, leaving the enlarged speedup claims insufficiently controlled.
